action: INCIBE-CERT advises assessing who can install firmware on the SPI flash and by what routes, since on some systems it can be updated without physical access; see AMD bulletin AMD-SB-7075 for platform scope. AMD does not plan a fix.
date_note: Date is INCIBE's publication date; AMD's own release date was not read.
exec: A critical, permanent flaw in the boot ROM of older AMD processors cannot be patched, so the risk has to be managed by controlling who can modify firmware storage.
plain: A flaw in the boot code of first-generation AMD Zen and Zen+ chips lets someone who can rewrite the firmware chip run unsigned code. AMD will not fix it.

key_findings: CVE-2026-74127: the PSP boot ROM in AMD Zen 1 and Zen+ (Zeppelin) processors verifies firmware signatures incorrectly.
An attacker able to modify the SPI flash could run unsigned firmware with the security processor's highest privileges.
INCIBE rates it critical and lists exploitation as No; reported by Matteo Rizzo of Google.
AMD does not plan a fix or mitigation because the boot ROM is immutable.
recommendations: Assess who can install firmware on the SPI flash and by what routes; on some systems it can be updated without physical access.
Consult AMD bulletin AMD-SB-7075 for platform scope.

summary: INCIBE-CERT reports a critical flaw, CVE-2026-74127, in the boot ROM of the platform security processor in first-generation AMD Zen and Zen+ chips. An attacker with local write access to the SPI flash could run unsigned firmware with the processor's top privileges. INCIBE lists no known exploitation. AMD does not plan a fix because the ROM is immutable.
title: AMD Zen and Zen+ boot ROM signature flaw cannot be patched, INCIBE warns
